answers 202, so the response does not reveal whether an account exists.

Verifies the credential `navigator.credentials.create()` made against the challenge from the
start, saves it and emails the owner. A challenge works once.

post.description:
Checks the password again and returns the options for `navigator.credentials.create()`. The
challenge stays on the server for five minutes, named by a cookie.

409.description: The account has as many passkeys as it may hold

post.description:
Verifies the credential `navigator.credentials.get()` returned against the challenge from the
start and starts a session for its owner, set as an `HttpOnly` cookie. Passkeys always verify
the user, by PIN or biometrics, so this sign-in needs no second step. A challenge works once.

401.description: Unknown passkey, failed verification, or the sign-in expired or already finished

403.description: The address is not verified yet

delete.description:
Checks the password again, deletes one of the signed-in user's passkeys and emails the owner.
Answers 404 for a passkey that is not theirs.

Emails a new verification link when the address belongs to an unverified account. Always
answers 202, so the response does not reveal whether an account exists.

429.description: Too many writes from this client

post.description:
Spends the token from a reset email and sets the new password. Every session, sign-in waiting
for a second factor and other emailed link of the account stops working, so the user signs in
again everywhere.

400.description: Invalid or breached password, or the link is malformed, expired or already used

429.description: Too many writes from this client

retry-after.description: Seconds until another attempt is allowed

get.description: The signed-in user, or `null`. Reading it also keeps an active session from expiring.

post.description:
Starts a session for a verified account and sets it as an `HttpOnly` cookie. With two-step
verification on, answers `two_factor_required` instead and sets a cookie that
`POST /signin/two-factor` needs within five minutes to finish the sign-in.

set-cookie.description: The session cookie, or the one that carries the sign-in to its second factor

403.description: The address is not verified yet

429.description: Too many attempts from this client or at this account

retry-after.description: Seconds until another attempt is allowed

post.description:
Completes a sign-in that `POST /signin` answered with `two_factor_required`, using a code from
the authenticator app or a recovery code. Each code works once. After five wrong codes the
sign-in ends and has to start over from the password. An account gets five codes checked, then
one every 30 minutes, however many sign-ins they are spread over.

400.description: The code is wrong or was used already

401.description: No sign-in is waiting: it expired, ran out of attempts or never started

429.description: Too many writes from this client, or codes tried for this account

retry-after.description: Seconds until another attempt is allowed

post.description: Ends the current session and clears its cookie. Answers 204 even when nobody was signed in.

429.description: Too many writes from this client

retry-after.description: Seconds until another attempt is allowed

Creates an account and emails a link to verify its address. Signing in waits until the
address is verified.

set-cookie.description: Marks this browser, so the verification link signs it in

400.description: Invalid email, or an invalid or breached password

429.description: Too many writes from this client

retry-after.description: Seconds until another attempt is allowed

get.description:
Whether signing in asks for a code from an authenticator app, and how many recovery codes are
left.

post.description:
Checks the password, then deletes the authenticator key and every recovery code, so signing in
asks for the password alone again.

Confirms the pending key with a code from the authenticator app, after which signing in asks
for a code too. Returns ten recovery codes, each good for one sign-in without the app. Every
session of the account ends, this one included, and this browser gets a new one, so a session
someone else may already hold does not outlast the change.

409.description: Already on, or the setup was never started

post.description:
Checks the password, then returns ten new recovery codes. The earlier ones stop working, used
or not.

Checks the password, then creates a key for an authenticator app. Signing in does not ask for
codes until `POST /two-factor/enable` confirms the app shows the right one. Starting again
replaces a key that was never confirmed.

Spends the token from a verification email and marks the address verified. The browser that
signed up is signed in as well; any other browser has to sign in afterwards.

set-cookie.description: The session cookie, for the browser that signed up

400.description: The link is malformed, expired or already used

429.description: Too many writes from this client

retry-after.description: Seconds until another attempt is allowed

get.description: Reports whether the database is reachable

code.description: The 6-digit code the authenticator app shows

ConfirmPasskeyChange.description: The account password, asked again before a passkey is added or removed

EmailToken.description: The token from an emailed link

signed_in.description: Only the browser that signed up is signed in by the link; any other has to sign in

version.description: Lets a deploy tell when the new release is the one answering

name.description: Tells the user's passkeys apart; blank or left out, it is "Passkey"

PasskeyRequestOptions.description:
Options for `navigator.credentials.get()`. They name no account, so the browser offers every
passkey it holds for this site; the page picks the mediation, modal or conditional.

last_used_at.description: `null` until the passkey first signs in

PasswordConfirmation.description: The account password, asked again before a change to two-step verification

token.description: The token from the reset email's link

recovery_code.description: One of the codes saved when two-step verification was turned on

recovery_codes.description:
Each signs in once in place of an authenticator code. The server keeps only their hashes,
so this response is the one time they are shown.

SecondFactor.description: The second step of a sign-in: a code from the authenticator app, or a recovery code

SignInResponse.description:
With two-step verification on, the password only starts the sign-in, and
`POST /signin/two-factor` finishes it

TwoFactorSetup.description: What an authenticator app needs to start showing codes for the account

otpauth_url.description: Adds the account to an app that opens `otpauth://` links

qr_code.description: `otpauth_url` as a QR code: an SVG image in a `data:` URL

secret.description: The key in base32, for typing into an app by hand

recovery_codes_remaining.description: Unused recovery codes; 0 while two-step verification is off
